questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: UBC is a well known and high rated university which was a great aspect in my choice. Further UBC has a green profile and are one of the leading universities in terms of studying the climate change mitigation. Further the mix of north American (as well as native) culture and the nature of Canada/Vancouver, was a great motivator.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Graduate courses in Economics is restricted for exchange students, which meant that not all of my courses was super interesting/difficult. I would recommend looking at graduate courses anyway, found out too late that it can be possible to get graduate courses, but takes sometime taking to the professor, Go Global, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: All information upon arrival was pretty easy to find (mostly UBC webpage and Go Global emails)

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Missed the intro-day so not much really. Got some assistance from follow exchange students

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: On campus housing was somewhat restricted, since most UBC students did not go on exchange (due to covid) leaving less room for incoming exchange students. I was randomly selected. Had many options to apply for housing, got my 1st priority (Fairview Crescent). There are usually many exchange students in Fairview Crescent making it a very social place to live. Since there was less exchange students it was less social this year. The buildings are not new, so don't expect anything fancy.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: Meal plan was available, but the house had kitchen so did not use it. The kitchen (as well as room) was not equipped at all, so had to buy all new things with my roommates. Try to find used equipment, maybe from other exchange student students to save some money.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It is nice to live on campus and not have to use up to 2 hours in public transport everyday. But it also means you don't use the city (especially downtown) as much as others would do.

Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer:
Get nominated by KU --> Apply to UBC --> Apply for courses and housing 
Fairly easy and a lot of help from KU.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Mostly from KU and UBC website/ GO global

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Had to prioritize 10 courses, did not get my top 4, but could choose again upon arrival, ended up with all my top courses.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start the process early, takes some time.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Graduate courses in Economics is restricted, but try anyway.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 400 level courses are fine to take as a MA student. Had one 300 course which was a bit too easy/boring. Had one neighbor-course in political science. It was nice to try something else.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: More high-school style. Smaller classes and more involved. Exams are only 30-40% of grade, so assignments, quizzes, and participation also counts towards the grade.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
ECON 339 - Economics of Technological Change
ECON 455 - International Trade
ECON 472 - Economics of Renewable Resources
POLI 366 - International Political Economy

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
ECON 455 was a good course, ECON 472 was also fine but mostly about fishing as renewable resources
POLI 366 was also good if you are interested in politics and international relations

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer:
A lot of recreational opportunities at UBC. 
Nature is so nice, go hiking, surfing, skiing etc.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Use UBC recreational (team)sports to meet new people.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Take a dive into the natives and try to learn about it. It is a surprisingly big part of everyday life.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Nature, nature, nature
Vancouver Island, Garabaldi, Whislter, Banff/Jasper, Okanagan, Washington

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Use recreation and clubs to meet locals. Especially the clubs weekend trips, ski-trip/surf-trip etc.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Openness, kindness and helpfulness

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Dont waste too much time on school and homework :)) Go live your life and make some memories, it is over before you realize it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: I think everything is provided

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting new people

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Getting stuck with a bus in a flooding and getting covid

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
